claims.title: Requests package provides a high-level HTTP client with session and adapter architecture
claims.text: The Requests library is architected around a Session class that manages persistent HTTP connections, cookies, and configuration, and uses transport adapters like HTTPAdapter to handle connection pooling, retries, and proxy management. The main request flow involves creating a Request, preparing it into a PreparedRequest, sending it via a Session which delegates to an appropriate Adapter, and returning a Response object. Core modules include sessions for session management, adapters for connection handling, models for request/response objects, and utils for helper functions.

claims.title: Session merges user and environment settings, manages redirects, authentication, and hooks
claims.text: The Session class merges per-request settings with session defaults and environment variables, supports .netrc authentication, manages cookies, handles redirects with careful header and auth rebuilding, and dispatches hooks on responses. It maintains adapters keyed by URL prefixes and supports mounting custom adapters. The send method orchestrates sending PreparedRequests, handling proxies, SSL verification, and response processing including cookie extraction and redirect following.

claims.title: HTTPAdapter manages connection pools with urllib3, supports proxies including SOCKS, and SSL certificate verification
claims.text: HTTPAdapter uses urllib3's PoolManager and ProxyManager to manage connection pools and retries. It supports proxy URLs including SOCKS proxies, caches proxy managers, and builds connection pool keys based on SSL context and certificates. It verifies SSL certificates with error handling for missing files and constructs Response objects from urllib3 responses. Deprecated methods warn users to migrate to newer APIs.

claims.title: Models module defines Request and Response objects with support for URL preparation, body encoding, authentication, and streaming responses
claims.text: The models module provides Request and Response classes that handle URL preparation including IDNA encoding, body preparation supporting JSON and multipart files, authentication application, and response content streaming with chunk and line iteration. Response objects support raising for HTTP errors, closing connections, and decoding JSON with error wrapping.

claims.title: Utilities module provides environment proxy resolution, header validation, URL manipulation, and other helper functions
claims.text: The utils module contains functions for proxy environment variable handling, proxy bypass logic including Windows registry support, header validation to prevent invalid headers, URL manipulation utilities like requote_uri and urldefragauth, and helpers for content length calculation and JSON encoding detection. It also includes context managers for environment variable management and atomic file writes.

claims.title: Compatibility and internal utilities modules provide backward compatibility and internal helpers
claims.text: The compat module maintains backward compatibility between Python versions and resolves character detection libraries. The _internal_utils module provides internal helpers such as header validation regexes and string conversion utilities. These modules support the core functionality without exposing complex dependencies.

claims.title: Exceptions module defines a hierarchy of exceptions with rich context for HTTP and JSON errors
claims.text: The exceptions module defines RequestException as a base with optional request and response attributes, specialized exceptions for connection, timeout, and HTTP errors, and a JSONDecodeError that preserves JSON error details and supports serialization. It combines built-in exceptions with request-specific context for precise error handling.

claims.title: Hooks module implements a simple event hook system focused on response hooks
claims.text: The hooks module defines a single hook event type "response" and provides functions to create default empty hooks and dispatch hooks by calling registered callables with the response data. This allows users to register callbacks to modify or inspect responses before they are returned.

claims.title: Tests are organized to cover core functionality including adapters, sessions, requests, utilities, and server behavior
claims.text: The tests directory contains modules testing adapters, hooks, low-level HTTP behaviors, packages exposure, requests API, structures like CaseInsensitiveDict, utilities including proxy and environment handling, and a test server implementation for integration tests. Tests use fixtures, parametrization, and mock servers to verify correctness and regression prevention.

claims.title: check_compatibility function verifies versions of urllib3 and character encoding libraries
claims.text: The check_compatibility function in src/requests/__init__.py validates that the installed versions of urllib3, chardet, and charset_normalizer meet minimum and maximum version requirements, raising assertions or issuing warnings if incompatible versions are detected.

claims.title: _check_cryptography warns about old cryptography versions
claims.text: The _check_cryptography function in src/requests/__init__.py parses the cryptography library version and issues a RequestsDependencyWarning if the version is older than 1.3.4, indicating potential performance slowdowns.

claims.title: Conditional import and fallback to pyopenssl for SNI support
claims.text: src/requests/__init__.py attempts to import the ssl module and checks for SNI support. If SNI is not supported, it injects pyopenssl into urllib3 as a fallback and checks the cryptography version for compatibility.

claims.title: Imports and exposes core API functions, exceptions, models, and session objects
claims.text: The module imports and exposes HTTP method functions (get, post, put, etc.) from .api, exception classes from .exceptions, request/response models from .models, and session management from .sessions, making them available at the package level.

claims.title: Configures warnings and logging to avoid noisy output
claims.text: The module silences urllib3 DependencyWarnings by default, sets a NullHandler on its logger to prevent 'No handler found' warnings, and sets FileModeWarning to default behavior, controlling the verbosity of warnings and logging.

claims.title: unicode_is_ascii checks if a unicode string contains only ASCII characters
claims.text: The function unicode_is_ascii(u_string) asserts that the input is a unicode string (str) and returns True if it can be encoded to ASCII without error, otherwise False.

claims.title: unicode_is_ascii enforces input type with assertion
claims.text: unicode_is_ascii uses an assert statement to ensure the input is a unicode string (str), explicitly excluding Python 2 str types, before attempting ASCII encoding.

claims.title: Module purpose and imports in src/requests/adapters.py
claims.text: The module src/requests/adapters.py defines transport adapters used by Requests to manage HTTP and HTTPS connections, importing urllib3 components for connection pooling, retries, and exceptions, as well as internal Requests utilities for authentication, cookies, and URL handling.

claims.title: Definition of BaseAdapter class with abstract methods
claims.text: The BaseAdapter class in src/requests/adapters.py serves as an abstract base class for transport adapters, defining the interface methods send and close which raise NotImplementedError and must be implemented by subclasses.

claims.title: HTTPAdapter class manages connection pools and retries using urllib3
claims.text: The HTTPAdapter class in src/requests/adapters.py extends BaseAdapter to provide an HTTP transport adapter that manages connection pools and retries using urllib3's PoolManager and Retry classes, with configurable pool size, blocking behavior, and retry policies.

claims.title: HTTPAdapter supports proxy management including SOCKS proxies
claims.text: HTTPAdapter in src/requests/adapters.py maintains a proxy_manager cache and returns appropriate urllib3 ProxyManager instances for proxies, including SOCKS proxies via SOCKSProxyManager if the proxy URL starts with 'socks'.

claims.title: HTTPAdapter cert_verify method validates SSL certificates with error handling
claims.text: The cert_verify method of HTTPAdapter verifies SSL certificates for HTTPS URLs, supports custom CA bundles or directories, raises OSError if certificate files or directories are missing, and configures the urllib3 connection's cert_reqs, ca_certs, cert_file, and key_file accordingly.

claims.title: HTTPAdapter builds Response objects from urllib3 responses
claims.text: The build_response method of HTTPAdapter constructs a Requests Response object from a urllib3 response, setting status code, headers, encoding, raw response, URL, cookies, and linking the original request and connection adapter.

claims.title: build_connection_pool_key_attributes builds urllib3 PoolKey attributes
claims.text: The method build_connection_pool_key_attributes in src/requests/adapters.py constructs the PoolKey attributes used by urllib3 to select a connection from a connection pool. It uses the PreparedRequest, verify parameter, and cert parameter to determine SSL-related keys such as ssl_context, cert_reqs, ca_certs, ca_cert_dir, cert_file, and key_file.

claims.title: get_connection_with_tls_context returns a urllib3 connection with TLS settings
claims.text: The method get_connection_with_tls_context returns a urllib3 connection for a given PreparedRequest and TLS settings including verify, proxies, and cert. It selects a proxy if applicable, builds connection pool key attributes, validates proxy URLs, and obtains a connection from either a proxy manager or the main pool manager.

claims.title: get_connection is deprecated in favor of get_connection_with_tls_context
claims.text: The method get_connection is deprecated and issues a DeprecationWarning advising users to migrate to get_connection_with_tls_context. It returns a urllib3 connection for a given URL and proxies, validating proxy URLs and using either a proxy manager or the main pool manager to obtain the connection.

claims.title: proxy_headers returns Proxy-Authorization header if proxy URL has credentials
claims.text: The proxy_headers method returns a dictionary of headers to add to requests sent through a proxy. If the proxy URL contains a username, it adds a Proxy-Authorization header with basic authentication credentials.

claims.title: request_url returns full URL for proxied HTTP requests except SOCKS proxies
claims.text: The request_url method returns the URL to use when making the final request. If the request is proxied over HTTP (not HTTPS) and not using a SOCKS proxy, it returns the full URL including scheme and host; otherwise, it returns only the path portion of the URL.

claims.title: requests.api module provides HTTP request methods
claims.text: The src/requests/api.py file defines functions for HTTP methods such as request, get, options, head, post, put, patch, and delete, which construct and send HTTP requests using the sessions.Session class.

claims.title: request function uses sessions.Session context manager to send requests
claims.text: The request function in src/requests/api.py creates a new sessions.Session object using a with statement to ensure the session is closed after the request, then calls session.request with the given method, url, and kwargs.

claims.title: head function disables redirects by default
claims.text: In src/requests/api.py, the head function sets allow_redirects to False by default in kwargs before calling the generic request function, differing from the default True in other methods.

claims.title: _basic_auth_str function creates Basic Auth header string with backward compatibility warnings
claims.text: The _basic_auth_str function in src/requests/auth.py returns a Basic Authentication header string, encoding username and password as latin1 bytes and base64 encoding them. It warns about non-string username and password inputs for backward compatibility, which will be removed in version 3.0.0.

claims.title: HTTPDigestAuth resets 401 call counter on redirects and limits retry attempts
claims.text: The HTTPDigestAuth class resets its internal 401 call counter when handling redirects and limits digest authentication retries to avoid infinite loops by checking the number of 401 responses processed per thread.

claims.title: HTTPBasicAuth and HTTPProxyAuth classes attach respective Authorization headers
claims.text: The HTTPBasicAuth class attaches an HTTP Basic Authorization header to requests, while HTTPProxyAuth inherits from it and attaches a Proxy-Authorization header instead, both using the _basic_auth_str function.

claims.title: Module provides default CA certificate bundle location
claims.text: The src/requests/certs.py module is responsible for returning the preferred default CA certificate bundle location, which is provided by the certifi package's where() function.

claims.title: Imports where function from certifi package
claims.text: The module imports the where function from the certifi package to determine the location of the CA certificate bundle.

claims.text: The module's docstring notes that if packaging Requests for a managed environment, the definition of where() can be changed to return a different CA bundle location, enabling customization of the CA certificates used.

claims.title: Prints CA bundle location when run as main program
claims.text: When executed as the main program, src/requests/certs.py prints the path to the CA certificate bundle by calling where().

claims.title: Module purpose and compatibility role
claims.text: The src/requests/compat.py module is responsible for maintaining backwards compatibility between Python 2 and Python 3, especially for the requests library, and it currently serves as a legacy compatibility layer until the next major version of requests.

claims.title: Character detection library resolution
claims.text: The function _resolve_char_detection in src/requests/compat.py attempts to import character detection libraries in order, first trying 'chardet' then 'charset_normalizer', returning the first successfully imported module or None if neither is available.

claims.title: urllib3 version detection logic
claims.text: The module imports urllib3's version string and sets a boolean is_urllib3_1 to True if the major version is 1, or defaults to True if the version cannot be parsed due to TypeError or AttributeError, preferring old functionality in that case.

claims.title: JSON module import with fallback and error class aliasing
claims.text: The module tries to import simplejson as json and sets has_simplejson accordingly; if simplejson is unavailable, it falls back to the built-in json module. It also imports JSONDecodeError from whichever json module is used to maintain consistent error handling.

claims.title: Legacy urllib imports for URL and proxy utilities
claims.text: The module imports various URL parsing and proxy-related functions from urllib.parse and urllib.request respectively, maintaining legacy import paths for compatibility.

claims.title: Python version detection flags
claims.text: The module defines boolean flags is_py2 and is_py3 based on sys.version_info to detect whether the runtime Python version is 2.x or 3.x, aiding conditional compatibility logic.

claims.title: MockRequest class adapts requests.Request for http.cookiejar compatibility
claims.text: The MockRequest class wraps a requests.Request object to provide an interface compatible with http.cookiejar.CookieJar, implementing methods like get_type, get_host, get_full_url, and header management to support cookie policy enforcement.

claims.title: extract_cookies_to_jar extracts cookies from urllib3 response to CookieJar
claims.text: The function extract_cookies_to_jar takes a CookieJar, a requests.Request, and a urllib3.HTTPResponse, and extracts cookies from the response's original HTTPMessage into the CookieJar using MockRequest and MockResponse wrappers.

claims.title: RequestsCookieJar handles cookie value quoting in set_cookie
claims.text: RequestsCookieJar overrides set_cookie to remove surrounding double quotes from cookie values if present before storing the cookie, ensuring cookie values are normalized.

claims.title: MockRequest raises NotImplementedError for add_header method
claims.text: The MockRequest class explicitly raises NotImplementedError if add_header is called, indicating cookiejar should use add_unredirected_header instead for adding cookie headers.

claims.title: _find_no_duplicates method finds a unique cookie value by name, domain, and path
claims.text: The _find_no_duplicates method in src/requests/cookies.py iterates over cookies to find a unique cookie matching the given name, optional domain, and optional path. It raises a CookieConflictError if multiple matching cookies exist, and raises KeyError if none are found, returning the cookie's value otherwise.

claims.title: RequestsCookieJar supports pickling by customizing __getstate__ and __setstate__
claims.text: The RequestsCookieJar class in src/requests/cookies.py overrides __getstate__ and __setstate__ to make instances pickleable by removing the unpickleable _cookies_lock attribute before pickling and restoring it after unpickling.

claims.title: copy method returns a new RequestsCookieJar with the same cookies and policy
claims.text: The copy method of RequestsCookieJar creates a new RequestsCookieJar instance, copies the cookie policy from the original, updates it with all cookies from the original jar, and returns the new jar.

claims.title: create_cookie constructs a cookielib.Cookie with default attributes and validates kwargs
claims.text: The create_cookie function builds a cookielib.Cookie object from a name, value, and optional keyword arguments. It sets default attributes such as domain as empty string, path as '/', discard as True, and validates that no unexpected keyword arguments are passed, raising TypeError if so.

claims.title: morsel_to_cookie converts a Morsel object to a Cookie, handling max-age and expires
claims.text: The morsel_to_cookie function converts an http.cookies.Morsel object into a cookielib.Cookie, calculating the expires attribute from max-age or expires string, raising TypeError if max-age is not an integer, and mapping other Morsel attributes to cookie parameters.

claims.title: merge_cookies merges cookies from dict or CookieJar into a CookieJar with type checks
claims.text: The merge_cookies function adds cookies from a dictionary or another CookieJar into a target CookieJar. It raises ValueError if the target is not a CookieJar, uses cookiejar_from_dict for dict input, and tries to update or individually set cookies for CookieJar input.

claims.title: RequestException stores optional request and response objects
claims.text: The RequestException class constructor accepts optional 'request' and 'response' keyword arguments, storing them as instance attributes. If only a response is provided and it has a 'request' attribute, the request attribute is set from the response.

claims.title: JSONDecodeError inherits from both InvalidJSONError and CompatJSONDecodeError to preserve JSON error details
claims.text: The JSONDecodeError class inherits from InvalidJSONError and CompatJSONDecodeError, and its constructor initializes both base classes to preserve JSON-specific error arguments and messages. It also overrides __reduce__ to ensure correct pickling behavior by delegating to CompatJSONDecodeError's __reduce__.

claims.title: Timeout exceptions have a hierarchy distinguishing connection and read timeouts
claims.text: Timeout is a base exception for timeouts, with ConnectTimeout inheriting from both ConnectionError and Timeout to indicate connection-specific timeouts, and ReadTimeout inheriting from Timeout to indicate server read timeouts. Catching Timeout will catch both connect and read timeout errors.

claims.title: Several exceptions combine RequestException with built-in exceptions for specific error semantics
claims.text: Exceptions like MissingSchema, InvalidSchema, InvalidURL, and InvalidHeader inherit from RequestException and built-in exceptions like ValueError or TypeError to provide more specific error semantics related to URL and header validation errors.

claims.title: _implementation() returns Python implementation name and version
claims.text: The _implementation() function returns a dictionary with the current Python implementation name and version, handling CPython, PyPy, Jython, IronPython, and defaults to 'Unknown' if unrecognized.

claims.title: info() collects detailed environment and library version info with error handling
claims.text: The info() function gathers platform system and release info with OSError handling, Python implementation info, and versions of urllib3, charset_normalizer, chardet, pyOpenSSL, cryptography, idna, and requests, returning a comprehensive dictionary.

claims.title: Module conditionally imports optional dependencies and handles missing imports gracefully
claims.text: The module attempts to import charset_normalizer, chardet, and pyopenssl with try-except blocks, setting them to None if unavailable, allowing the info() function to report their presence and versions accordingly.

claims.title: main() prints the bug report info as pretty-formatted JSON when run as script
claims.text: The main() function pretty-prints the dictionary returned by info() as JSON with sorted keys and indentation, and is executed if the module is run as the main program.

claims.title: Module provides hooks system for Requests library
claims.text: The src/requests/hooks.py module defines a hooks system specifically for the Requests library, with currently only one hook type named "response" which is triggered by the response generated from a Request.

claims.title: HOOKS list defines available hook events
claims.text: The HOOKS list in src/requests/hooks.py contains the string "response", indicating that the only supported hook event currently is "response".

claims.title: default_hooks function returns dictionary with empty lists for each hook event
claims.text: The default_hooks function returns a dictionary where each key is a hook event from HOOKS and each value is an empty list, representing no registered hooks by default.

claims.title: dispatch_hook function executes hooks for a given event key and updates hook_data
claims.text: The dispatch_hook function takes a key, a hooks dictionary, and hook_data, then calls each hook registered under the key with hook_data and additional kwargs. If a hook returns a non-None value, hook_data is updated to that value before returning it.

claims.title: dispatch_hook supports single callable or list of callables as hooks
claims.text: In dispatch_hook, if the hooks object for a key is a single callable (not a list), it is wrapped into a list to allow uniform iteration over hooks.

claims.title: Module imports and dependencies in src/requests/models.py
claims.text: The module imports various utilities and exceptions from urllib3, internal utilities, compatibility helpers, cookie handling, exceptions, hooks, status codes, structures, and utility functions from the requests package, indicating it is a core part of the Requests library handling HTTP requests and responses.

claims.title: RequestHooksMixin manages registration and deregistration of event hooks
claims.text: The RequestHooksMixin class provides methods to register and deregister hooks for specific events. It validates event names, supports single callable hooks or iterables of callables, and handles errors gracefully by returning False if a hook to deregister does not exist.

claims.title: _get_idna_encoded_host encodes hostnames using IDNA with error handling
claims.text: The static method _get_idna_encoded_host in src/requests/models.py uses the idna library to encode a hostname with UTS46 processing, decoding it back to UTF-8, and raises a UnicodeError if the encoding fails.

claims.title: prepare_url validates and constructs HTTP URLs with IDNA encoding and query parameter handling
claims.text: The prepare_url method in src/requests/models.py prepares an HTTP URL by decoding bytes, stripping whitespace, parsing the URL components, validating scheme and host presence, encoding the host with IDNA if non-ASCII, reconstructing the netloc, encoding parameters, and recombining all parts into a properly quoted URL string.

claims.title: prepare_body handles various body types including JSON, streams, files, and sets appropriate headers
claims.text: The prepare_body method in src/requests/models.py prepares the HTTP request body by supporting JSON serialization with error handling, detecting streaming bodies and managing file positions, encoding multipart files, setting content-type headers, and preparing content-length headers accordingly.

claims.title: prepare_auth supports extracting auth from URL and applying HTTPBasicAuth tuples
claims.text: The prepare_auth method in src/requests/models.py prepares HTTP authentication by extracting credentials from the URL if auth is None, converting 2-tuple auth to HTTPBasicAuth, applying the auth callable to the request, updating the request's attributes, and recalculating content-length.

claims.title: Response.iter_content streams response data in chunks
claims.text: The method Response.iter_content in src/requests/models.py allows iteration over the response data in chunks of a specified size, supporting streaming large responses without loading all content into memory. It handles special cases for urllib3 raw responses and raises specific exceptions for protocol, decoding, timeout, and SSL errors.

claims.title: Response.iter_lines yields response content line by line
claims.text: The method Response.iter_lines in src/requests/models.py iterates over the response content one line at a time, optionally decoding unicode and splitting by a custom delimiter. It buffers partial lines across chunks to yield complete lines and is not reentrant safe.

claims.title: Response.content property returns response content as bytes and caches it
claims.text: The Response.content property returns the full response content as bytes, reading it lazily if not already consumed. It raises a RuntimeError if content is accessed after consumption and handles cases where the response has no raw data or status code 0 by returning None.

claims.title: Response.text property decodes response content to unicode with fallback
claims.text: The Response.text property decodes the response content to a unicode string using the response encoding or an apparent encoding if none is set. It handles encoding lookup errors by falling back to a replacement decode to avoid exceptions.

claims.title: Response.json decodes JSON content with encoding detection and error wrapping
claims.text: The Response.json method decodes the response body as JSON, attempting to detect UTF encodings per RFC 4627 if no encoding is set. It wraps JSON decoding errors in a RequestsJSONDecodeError and falls back to decoding from the text property if needed.

claims.title: Response.raise_for_status raises HTTPError for 4xx and 5xx status codes
claims.text: The Response.raise_for_status method raises an HTTPError if the response status code indicates a client (4xx) or server (5xx) error. It decodes the reason phrase from bytes using utf-8 or iso-8859-1 and includes the status code, reason, and URL in the error message.

claims.title: Response.close releases connection and prevents further raw access
claims.text: The Response.close method releases the underlying connection back to the pool and closes the raw response if content was not consumed. After calling close, the raw object should not be accessed. It also calls a release_conn method on raw if available.

claims.title: Backwards compatibility imports for urllib3 and idna
claims.text: The src/requests/packages.py file imports the urllib3 and idna packages dynamically and then maps their modules into the requests.packages namespace to preserve identity, enabling backwards compatibility.

claims.title: Conditional import and remapping of chardet package
claims.text: If the chardet package is available (not None), src/requests/packages.py remaps its modules into the requests.packages namespace similarly to urllib3 and idna, including an additional alias with the module name replaced by 'chardet'.

claims.title: Use of sys.modules to preserve module identity under requests.packages
claims.text: The code in src/requests/packages.py iterates over sys.modules to assign existing modules to new keys prefixed with 'requests.packages.', ensuring that requests.packages.urllib3.* and requests.packages.idna.* refer to the same module objects as urllib3.* and idna.* respectively.

claims.title: Imports chardet from local compat module
claims.text: The src/requests/packages.py file imports chardet from a local compat module, which may provide a fallback or compatibility layer for chardet.

claims.title: Code is explicitly for backwards compatibility and not recommended style
claims.text: The comments in src/requests/packages.py explicitly state that the code exists for backwards compatibility reasons and is not recommended style, indicating a design decision to maintain legacy support despite dislike for the approach.

claims.title: merge_setting and merge_hooks functions merge session and request settings
claims.text: The functions merge_setting and merge_hooks merge settings from individual requests with those from the session, handling dictionaries by combining keys and removing keys set to None, and properly merging hooks to avoid breaking session hooks when request hooks are empty lists.

claims.title: Session class provides a persistent HTTP session with cookie and connection management
claims.text: The Session class inherits from SessionRedirectMixin and represents a persistent HTTP session that manages cookies, connection pooling, and configuration such as headers, auth, proxies, hooks, and SSL verification. It supports usage as a context manager and maintains attributes like max_redirects and trust_env.

claims.title: rebuild_auth removes Authorization header on cross-host redirects and reapplies .netrc auth
claims.text: The rebuild_auth method removes the Authorization header from a redirected request if the redirect is to a different host to prevent credential leakage, and attempts to reapply authentication from .netrc if trust_env is enabled.

claims.title: rebuild_proxies updates proxy settings and Proxy-Authorization header on redirects
claims.text: The rebuild_proxies method recalculates proxy configuration considering environment variables and NO_PROXY settings, removes existing Proxy-Authorization headers, and adds new Proxy-Authorization headers for non-HTTPS schemes when proxy credentials are present.

claims.title: Session class initializes default HTTP session settings
claims.text: The code defines an __init__ method (lines 390-450) that initializes default settings for an HTTP session, including headers, authentication, proxies, hooks, query parameters, SSL verification, client certificates, redirect limits, environment trust, cookies, and connection adapters.

claims.title: prepare_request method merges session and request settings into a PreparedRequest
claims.text: The prepare_request method (lines 457-498) takes a Request object and merges its settings with the Session's defaults, including cookies, authentication (with netrc support if trust_env is True), headers, parameters, and hooks, returning a PreparedRequest ready for sending.

claims.title: Convenience methods for HTTP verbs call request with appropriate defaults
claims.text: Methods get, options, head, post, put, patch, and delete (lines 593-671) provide convenient wrappers around the request method, setting HTTP method and defaults like allow_redirects accordingly.

claims.title: send method sends a PreparedRequest and handles redirects, cookies, and hooks
claims.text: The send method (lines 673-748) sends a PreparedRequest using an appropriate adapter, manages default parameters like stream, verify, cert, resolves proxies, raises an error if a Request (not PreparedRequest) is passed, measures elapsed time, dispatches response hooks, extracts cookies from responses, handles redirects if allowed, and optionally loads response content immediately if not streaming.

claims.title: merge_environment_settings merges environment variables with session settings
claims.text: The merge_environment_settings method (lines 750-780) merges proxies, stream, verify, and cert settings with environment variables if trust_env is True, including support for REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and CURL_CA_BUNDLE environment variables for SSL verification.

claims.title: Session.get_adapter returns the correct adapter for a URL or raises InvalidSchema
claims.text: The method get_adapter in the Session class iterates over registered adapters and returns the first adapter whose prefix matches the start of the given URL (case-insensitive). If no adapter matches, it raises an InvalidSchema exception indicating no connection adapters were found for the URL.

claims.title: Session.close closes all registered adapters
claims.text: The close method of the Session class calls the close method on all adapters stored in the adapters dictionary, effectively closing the session's connections.

claims.title: Session.mount registers a connection adapter and sorts adapters by prefix length
claims.text: The mount method registers a connection adapter to a given prefix in the adapters dictionary. It then reorders the adapters so that adapters with longer prefixes come before those with shorter prefixes by moving keys with shorter length to the end.

claims.title: Session supports pickling via __getstate__ and __setstate__ methods
claims.text: The Session class implements __getstate__ and __setstate__ methods to support pickling. __getstate__ returns a dictionary of attributes listed in __attrs__, and __setstate__ restores these attributes from the given state dictionary.

claims.title: Deprecated session() function returns a new Session instance

claims.text: The TestCaseInsensitiveDict class in tests/test_structures.py tests the CaseInsensitiveDict from requests.structures, verifying that keys are handled case-insensitively for getting, deleting, and equality, and also tests methods like lower_items, copy, and repr.

claims.title: TestLookupDict tests attribute-based dictionary lookup behavior
claims.text: The TestLookupDict class in tests/test_structures.py tests the LookupDict from requests.structures, ensuring that attribute keys can be accessed via dictionary-style getitem and get methods, and verifies the repr output.

claims.title: Tests use pytest fixtures and parameterization for setup and multiple key variants
claims.text: Both TestCaseInsensitiveDict and TestLookupDict use pytest fixtures with autouse=True for setup, initializing instances with preset data, and use pytest.mark.parametrize to test multiple key variants and expected results in test methods.

claims.title: CaseInsensitiveDict equality supports comparison with dict and None
claims.text: The test_instance_equality method in TestCaseInsensitiveDict verifies that the CaseInsensitiveDict instance compares equal to a dict with matching keys ignoring case, and returns False when compared to empty dict or None.

claims.title: LookupDict returns None for missing keys in getitem and get
claims.text: The TestLookupDict tests confirm that LookupDict returns None when accessing keys that are not present as attributes, both via __getitem__ and get methods.

claims.title: Tests verify Server context manager closes server and disallows new connections
claims.text: The test_server_closes method tests that the Server instance closes properly when exiting its context manager, and that new socket connections to the same host and port fail with socket.error after closure.

claims.title: Tests check Server's ability to serve multiple HTTP requests and limit connections
claims.text: The test_multiple_requests method verifies that the Server.basic_response_server can handle a specified number of HTTP requests successfully and that the next request after the limit raises a requests.exceptions.ConnectionError.

claims.title: Tests verify Server supports waiting for an event before closing
claims.text: The test_basic_waiting_server method demonstrates that the Server.basic_response_server can be configured to wait for a threading.Event (block_server) before closing, allowing multiple sends before the server is released to close.

claims.title: Tests confirm Server handles request timeouts and recovers request data
claims.text: The tests test_requests_after_timeout_are_not_received and test_request_recovery_with_bigger_timeout verify that Server.basic_response_server respects a request_timeout parameter, discarding requests sent after the timeout and correctly recovering request data sent before the timeout.

claims.title: Tests ensure Server thread exits cleanly on exceptions or no connections
claims.text: The test_server_finishes_on_error and test_server_finishes_when_no_connections methods confirm that the Server thread exits properly even if an exception is raised inside the context manager or if no connections are made, preventing test suite hangs.

claims.title: TestGetNetrcAuth validates get_netrc_auth function with environment variable and URL parsing
claims.text: The TestGetNetrcAuth class tests get_netrc_auth by creating a temporary .netrc file and setting the NETRC environment variable. It verifies correct extraction of login and password for a given URL and ensures that malformed URLs do not cause incorrect authentication retrieval.

claims.title: TestGetEnvironProxies checks proxy bypass logic based on no_proxy environment variable and argument
claims.text: The TestGetEnvironProxies class tests get_environ_proxies function to ensure IP addresses and hostnames listed in no_proxy environment variable or passed as argument correctly bypass proxies. It verifies that the no_proxy argument overrides the environment variable and tests various URLs for proxy bypass behavior.

claims.title: TestExtractZippedPaths verifies extraction of files from zip archives and handling of UNC paths
claims.text: The TestExtractZippedPaths class tests extract_zipped_paths function to confirm that paths inside zip files are extracted to temporary locations and that the function returns the original path unchanged for non-zip or invalid UNC paths. It uses temporary directories and compares extracted files to originals.

claims.title: Tests for guess_json_utf function with various encodings
claims.text: The test functions test_encoded, test_bad_utf_like_encoding, and test_guess_by_bom verify the behavior of the guess_json_utf function with different UTF encodings and BOMs, ensuring it correctly identifies or rejects encodings from byte data.

claims.title: Tests for URL authentication extraction
claims.text: The test_get_auth_from_url function tests the get_auth_from_url utility to correctly extract user and password credentials from various URL formats, including encoded characters and missing credentials.

claims.title: Tests for URI quoting and unquoting utilities
claims.text: The test functions test_requote_uri_with_unquoted_percents and test_unquote_unreserved validate the behavior of requote_uri and unquote_unreserved functions, ensuring correct handling of percent signs and reserved characters in URIs.

claims.title: Tests for proxy selection based on URL and proxy configuration
claims.text: The test_select_proxies function verifies that the select_proxy utility correctly chooses the appropriate proxy URL based on the input URL and different proxy dictionaries, handling case insensitivity and scheme variations.

claims.title: Tests for URL manipulation utilities
claims.text: The test functions test_prepend_scheme_if_needed, test_to_native_string, and test_urldefragauth verify utilities that prepend schemes to URLs, convert values to native strings, and remove authentication and fragment parts from URLs respectively.

claims.title: Tests for proxy bypass logic based on environment variables and URL
claims.text: The test_should_bypass_proxies and test_should_bypass_proxies_pass_only_hostname functions test the should_bypass_proxies utility, ensuring it respects environment variables NO_PROXY and no_proxy, correctly determines if proxies should be bypassed for given URLs, and calls proxy_bypass with hostname or IP without port or auth.

claims.title: Tests for add_dict_to_cookiejar with different CookieJar types
claims.text: The test function test_add_dict_to_cookiejar in tests/test_utils.py verifies that the add_dict_to_cookiejar function correctly adds cookies from a dictionary to both compat.cookielib.CookieJar and RequestsCookieJar instances.

claims.title: Tests for unicode_is_ascii function with various inputs
claims.text: The test function test_unicode_is_ascii in tests/test_utils.py checks that unicode_is_ascii returns True for ASCII strings and False for non-ASCII Unicode strings such as accented characters and Japanese text.

claims.title: Tests for should_bypass_proxies function with no_proxy argument
claims.text: The test function test_should_bypass_proxies_no_proxy in tests/test_utils.py verifies that should_bypass_proxies correctly determines whether to bypass proxies based on the no_proxy argument containing IP ranges and hostnames.

claims.title: Windows-specific tests for should_bypass_proxies using mocked Windows registry
claims.text: Several tests in tests/test_utils.py (test_should_bypass_proxies_win_registry, test_should_bypass_proxies_win_registry_bad_values, test_should_bypass_proxies_win_registry_ProxyOverride_value) mock Windows registry access via monkeypatching winreg to test should_bypass_proxies behavior with various ProxyEnable and ProxyOverride registry values, including valid, invalid, and semicolon-terminated override strings.

claims.title: Tests for set_environ context manager to set and restore environment variables
claims.text: The test functions test_set_environ and test_set_environ_raises_exception in tests/test_utils.py verify that the set_environ context manager correctly sets environment variables during the context and restores them afterward, and that it propagates exceptions raised inside the context when the value parameter is None.

claims.title: consume_socket_content reads all available data from a socket with timeout
claims.text: The function consume_socket_content(sock, timeout=0.5) reads data from the given socket in chunks of 65536 bytes until no more data is available or the timeout expires, returning the accumulated bytes content.

claims.title: Server class implements a threaded dummy server for unit testing
claims.text: The Server class extends threading.Thread and implements a dummy server that listens on a specified host and port, handles a fixed number of requests using a handler function, and supports synchronization via threading events for readiness and stopping.

claims.title: Server provides class methods for common HTTP response servers
claims.text: Server.text_response_server creates a Server instance with a handler that reads request content and sends a fixed text response; Server.basic_response_server creates a Server that responds with a minimal HTTP 200 OK response with no content.

claims.title: Server handles socket creation, binding, accepting connections, and error handling
claims.text: Server._create_socket_and_bind creates a TCP socket, binds it to the host and port, and listens; _accept_connection waits for incoming connections with a timeout and returns the accepted socket or None on timeout or error; _close_server_sock_ignore_errors closes the server socket ignoring OSError exceptions.

claims.title: Server supports context manager interface to start and stop the server thread safely
claims.text: Server.__enter__ starts the server thread and waits for it to be ready, raising RuntimeError on timeout; Server.__exit__ waits for the server to stop or signals it to stop on exceptions, closes the server socket to unblock accept calls, and joins the thread, allowing exceptions to propagate.

claims.title: TLSServer subclass extends Server to provide TLS support with optional mutual TLS
claims.text: TLSServer initializes an SSLContext with server certificate and key, optionally configures mutual TLS by setting verify_mode and loading CA certificates, and overrides _create_socket_and_bind to wrap the socket with SSL before binding and listening.

claims.title: override_environ context manager temporarily modifies environment variables
claims.text: The function override_environ in tests/utils.py is a context manager that temporarily overrides environment variables with the provided keyword arguments, restoring the original environment after the context exits.

claims.title: override_environ deletes environment variables if value is None
claims.text: Within override_environ, if a keyword argument's value is None, the corresponding environment variable is deleted from os.environ during the context.

claims.title: override_environ saves and restores the entire environment atomically
claims.text: override_environ saves a copy of the entire os.environ dictionary before modifications and restores it fully after the context, ensuring no side effects remain after use.
